analyst_view.overall: Early view: leaders Barcelona won 2-1 at Atlético through Fermín López but are without Rodri (hamstring, several weeks) and have doubts over Dani Olmo and Christensen. Villarreal's Íñigo Pérez faced an ultimatum from the club after a 0-6 Champions League defeat to PSG; one report says the 2-0 win over Getafe saved his job. Renato Veiga is suspended. Both clubs play away in the Champions League on Wednesday (Barça at Sabah, Villarreal at Slavia Prague).

goals.text: The numbers say 4.5 goals, which is very high. Barça scored six against Alavés, but a Villarreal side fighting for its coach's job reacted to the PSG thrashing with a clean sheet against Getafe and is likely to defend deep. Without Rodri, Barça also lose some control in midfield.

corners.text: The site expects 10.7 corners. If Pérez sits deep after the PSG game, Barça will have long spells in the final third, with Lamine Yamal and Fariñas attacking the right flank. Pressure like that usually brings plenty of blocked crosses and corners.

cards.text: The model has 4.4 cards. Teams chasing Barça on the counter tend to stop it with fouls (Atlético collected four yellows to Barça's one), and Villarreal lose Renato Veiga to a ban. Five cards looks reasonable.

shots.text: The site expects 28.2 shots. Barça at home against a deep block should be near 20 on their own, and Villarreal under Pérez still try to play out. Getting to 30 needs nothing unusual.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 on target and I am close to that. Barça's volume points up, but Olmo is a doubt and Villarreal's packed defence should block a lot, so I stay near the site's figure.
